scope: Ten existing Hong Kong taught MSc directory IDs gain first partial observations / twenty mode choices. Ten 2027/28 official catalogue pages, DDM requirements/fee/procedure pages and Business School priority page were consulted. No new programme, live application check or independent review.

records.academicNote: Information Systems, Operations Management, Statistics and related degrees are preferred, not a universal subject restriction. A satisfactory GMAT/GRE is strongly recommended without a published minimum. Relevant experience strengthens full-time applications; two relevant post-qualification full-time years are preferred for part-time study, not compulsory.

Either a science/engineering bachelor route, or another discipline with relevant computation work, at least one programming language, calculus and linear algebra preparation. All conditions in the alternative branch need assessment; no fixed work-year minimum is published. The undergraduate integrated pathway is restricted to qualifying HKUST students, not every applicant.

An Electrical, Electronic or Computer Engineering bachelor, or a related area, is required. The second-class honours wording belongs to the restricted HKUST integrated pathway, not ordinary MSc entry. Subject relevance and qualification equivalence remain assessed.

A bachelor in Mathematics, Engineering or Physical Sciences is required. Broad subject-family and qualification equivalence need assessment. The CGA 3.5 condition belongs only to the restricted HKUST integrated pathway, not generic MSc entry.

Programming/mathematics preparation is preferred; satisfactory GMAT/GRE is highly recommended without a numerical minimum. Full-time entry has no minimum work experience. Two full-time post-qualification work years are highly recommended for part-time applicants, not mandatory. An additional mathematics course may be required above the normal 30 credits.

Applicants should show a keen interest in information and cyber security management; computing, information systems, AI and data-analytics backgrounds are advantageous, not an exclusive subject gate. GMAT/GRE is highly recommended. Relevant experience adds weight for full-time study; two relevant full-time post-qualification years are an advantage for part-time study.

GRE/GMAT with satisfactory quantitative and verbal performance is recommended, without a numeric minimum. Work experience is advantageous for full-time applicants; two full-time post-qualification years are preferred for part-time study. The school may assign foundation courses for insufficient IS/computing/engineering preparation; no compulsory prior major or generic work-year threshold is inferred.

A bachelor in Computer Engineering, Computer Science or a related area is required. Recognition and subject relatedness need university assessment. Cybersecurity is an optional concentration within this MSc, not another master or a separate admission requirement.

Ordinary admission requires a second-class honours bachelor in Electronic Engineering, Engineering Science or Physical Sciences. Family-level qualification equivalence remains assessed. Second class is not narrowed to upper second, and a GPA is not converted to honours. The post-entry GGA 2.850 graduation criterion is not an admission GPA.

A bachelor in Electronic Engineering, Engineering, Physical Sciences or a related area is required. The integrated pathway has its own HKUST-year and second-class-equivalent conditions; they are not applied to ordinary entry. The six-credit project is part of taught study, not research-admission classification.
